cleanIntro: The Model 1854 field strips to three parts: the operating lever, the bolt assembly and the ejector. With those out, the bore is cleaned from the breech end, and the bolt, the lever and the inside of the receiver are cleaned and oiled on their own. Smith & Wesson stops there, so there is no Deep Clean for this rifle.

steps.title: Lever fully down and forward, without touching the trigger
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep your finger off the trigger. Grasp the operating lever and pull or push it down and fully forward until it stops. That opens the bolt, extracts and ejects any cartridge that was chambered, and cocks the hammer.
steps.prose: Opening the lever also engages the trigger block, which stays on until the lever is clicked fully closed again. Do not lean on that: the manual's rule is never to carry or handle this rifle with a cartridge in the chamber and the hammer resting on the bolt, so open the action before you do anything else with it.
steps.quote: Without touching the trigger, grasp the operating lever and pull/push it down and fully forward.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Unloading the Model 1854, Method One, for all models, p.31
steps.warn: NEVER CARRY, HANDLE OR TRANSPORT THE MODEL 1854 RIFLE WITH A CARTRIDGE IN THE CHAMBER AND THE HAMMER RESTING ON THE REAR OF THE BOLT WHERE THE FIRING PIN IS LOCATED.

steps.title: Cross-bolt safety fully right, to NO-FIRE
steps.action: With the action open, press the cross-bolt safety fully to the right, as viewed from above or from the rear, into the NO-FIRE position. The red o-ring on the safety should no longer show.
steps.prose: The safety only moves when the hammer is at half-cock or cocked, and opening the lever has just cocked it, so this is the moment it will go. It is a hammer block, not a trigger lock: it stops the hammer reaching the firing pin, but the trigger can still release the hammer, so keep your finger out of the guard.
steps.quote: Once the action is open, move the cross-bolt safety fully to the right into the “NO-FIRE” position (as viewed from above or from the rear)
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Unloading the Model 1854, Method One, for all models, p.31

steps.title: Cycle the lever until the tube, receiver and chamber are empty
steps.action: Look into the ejection port. If a cartridge is lying in the action, tip the rifle until it falls out through the port. Then keep cycling the lever, fully down and forward and then fully back and up, to feed and extract each cartridge from the magazine tube until the chamber, magazine and receiver are all empty.
steps.prose: Every stroke has to be a full one: close the lever completely, then open it completely, or a cartridge can be left behind or pushed back into the chamber. On a short-action rifle with the removable tube, the manual also lets you turn the tube to unlatch it and tip the cartridges out of the forend, but taking the tube out does not empty the chamber or the receiver, so you still look at both.
steps.quote: Continue to empty the magazine tube of cartridges by cycling the operating lever fully down and forward and then fully back and up
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Unloading the Model 1854, Method One, for all models, p.32
steps.warn: REMOVING THE MAGAZINE TUBE FROM THE “SHORT-ACTION” MODEL 1854 RIFLES DOES NOT UNLOAD THE CHAMBER OR RECEIVER.

steps.title: Look at the bolt face: the firing pin must not stick out
steps.action: With the action open and the rifle empty, look into the ejection port and make sure the firing pin is not protruding from the bolt face. If it is protruding, keep the rifle pointed in a safe direction, make sure it is unloaded, and have it inspected and test fired by a gunsmith qualified to work on Smith & Wesson firearms.
steps.prose: The manual asks for this check every time the rifle is cleaned, handed over, transported or stored. A firing pin that stays forward is a fault cleaning will not fix, and this is the one point in the routine where you can see it.
steps.quote: Look into the ejection port and ensure the firing pin is NOT protruding from the bolt face
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Inspecting the Model 1854, p.21
steps.warn: VERIFY THAT THE FIRING PIN IS NOT PROTRUDING FROM THE BOLT FACE.

steps.title: Three parts come out, and only three
steps.action: Leave the action open, lever down and forward. The operating lever, the bolt assembly and the ejector are the only action parts you take out of this rifle. The hammer, the trigger, the cross-bolt safety and the rest of the lockwork stay in the receiver.
steps.prose: Smith & Wesson draws the line here on purpose, and its general warning is never to take the rifle further apart than this procedure. Knowing the three parts before you start means you will not go looking for a fourth.
steps.quote: The operating lever, the bolt assembly and the ejector are the only action parts that should be removed from the rifle by the user.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.35

steps.title: Lever pivot screw out with a T20 Torx
steps.action: With the action open, remove the operating lever pivot screw from the frame with a T20 Torx screwdriver. Keep hold of the screw; it is the only fastener in the field strip.
steps.prose: Use the right bit. A worn or wrong-size driver will chew the screw head, and the same screw has to go back in snug at the end. If the lever is under tension and the screw will not come out freely, the manual's jam-clearing section says it may need a 5/32 inch or smaller punch from the side opposite the ejection port, with care for the threads in the trigger plate.
steps.quote: Remove the operating lever pivot screw from the frame using a T20 Torx® screwdriver
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.35

steps.title: Pull the operating lever down and out
steps.action: With the pivot screw out, pull the operating lever down and out of the receiver.
steps.prose: Look at the end of the lever as it comes out. It engages a slot at the front of the bolt, and getting that end back into that slot is the fiddly part of reassembly.
steps.quote: The operating lever can now be pulled down, out of the receiver once the pivot screw is removed
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.35

steps.title: Hold the hammer spur down and draw the bolt out the back
steps.action: Hold the hammer spur down firmly to take its tension off the bolt assembly, and pull the bolt rearward, out of the receiver.
steps.prose: If you do not hold the hammer down, it presses on the bolt and the bolt drags or binds on the way out. Hold the hammer the same way when the bolt goes back in.
steps.quote: Hold the hammer spur down firmly to relieve the tension against the bolt assembly (FIGURE 57) and pull the bolt rearward, out of the receiver.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.36

steps.title: Lift the ejector out through the ejection port
steps.action: Using tweezers or small needle-nose pliers, reach into the receiver through the ejection port and lift the ejector out of its recess. It sits inside the receiver, under where the bolt was.
steps.prose: The ejector is small and easy to drop inside the receiver, so grip it firmly before you lift. On reassembly a round extrusion on it engages a hole in the far side of the receiver, so notice which way it sits as it comes out.
steps.quote: reach into the receiver through the ejection port and lift out the ejector from its recess
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.36

steps.title: Short-action models: magazine tube out if it needs cleaning
steps.action: On a short-action rifle, the magazine tube can be unlatched by turning it counter-clockwise and withdrawn from under the barrel to be cleaned if it needs it. On a long-action rifle the tube is fastened in place and is not removable, so leave it alone.
steps.prose: This is the one step that depends on which Model 1854 you have. The long-action tube is fixed to the rifle; trying to turn or pull it does nothing useful and can damage it.
steps.quote: On the “short-action” models, the magazine tube can be unlatched and withdrawn from its position
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.36

steps.title: Threaded muzzle: thread protector off
steps.action: If your rifle has a threaded muzzle, take off the thread protector so the threads can be cleaned and lubricated. If it does not, skip this step.
steps.prose: Only some models have the threaded muzzle. Grit and fouling packed in the threads is what makes the protector hard to remove next time.
steps.quote: The thread protector on the muzzle (if rifle is so-equipped) can be removed and the threads cleaned and lubricated.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.37

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Operating lever, lever pivot screw, bolt assembly and ejector, plus the magazine tube on a short-action rifle and the thread protector if it has one. With these out, the bore can be cleaned from the breech end. The manual's field strip ends here and you should not take the rifle apart any further.
steps.prose: Smith & Wesson does not recommend any disassembly past this point, and it publishes no deeper procedure, so there is no Deep Clean for this rifle. If something needs attention beyond these parts, it goes to Smith & Wesson or a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For MODEL 1854 — p/n 3017061	
                           S&W_LAR_Manual_030125 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.37
steps.warn: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE DISASSEMBLY/FIELD STRIPPING PROCEDURE DETAILED IN THIS MANUAL

deepAbsentReason: The Model 1854 manual ends at the field strip. It names the operating lever, the bolt assembly and the ejector as the only action parts the user should remove (p.35), and after those, the magazine tube on short-action models and the thread protector, it states "No further disassembly is recommended." (p.37). Smith & Wesson publishes no deeper procedure for this rifle.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: With the bolt out, clean the bore from the breech end
Remove heavy firing residue from the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish with a dry cotton patch through the bore and chamber to take out the residue and solvent

After shooting 38 Special in a 357 Magnum rifle, or 44 Special in a 44 Rem Mag rifle, brush the front of the chamber thoroughly with solvent; the shorter cases leave a buildup there that causes extraction trouble with the full-length round
On a threaded muzzle, clean and lightly oil the threads before the thread protector goes back on

cleaning.name: BOLT, LEVER AND RECEIVER
tasks: Clean and lubricate the bolt assembly
Clean and lubricate the operating lever
Clean the internal surfaces of the receiver
On a short-action rifle, clean the magazine tube if it was taken out
Check every part for signs of wear; if wear is excessive, do not use the rifle until Smith & Wesson or a qualified gunsmith has seen it

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Clean the outside of the rifle with a non-abrasive cloth
Take off all cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints; finger moisture left on the metal can start corrosion
Do not use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this rifle
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION AND STORAGE
tasks: Put a single drop of good gun oil on each pivot point and bearing surface the manual shows
After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts inside and out with a high-quality firearm oil
Do not over-oil: too much oil attracts and holds dirt and gums up
In a cold climate use an oil that will not congeal
For long storage oil the bore, chamber and internal surfaces, coat the bolt and barrel with an anti-rust oil, and do not store the rifle in leather or heavy cloth or with a plug in the barrel
Clean the rifle again before it is next used after storage

reassembly: With tweezers or small needle-nose pliers, place the ejector into its recess in the receiver until the round extrusion on the ejector engages the hole in the far side of the receiver.
Look into the receiver: if the bolt locking lug has moved up, push it back down so the bolt can enter its channel.
Hold the hammer spur down and insert the bolt assembly about halfway into the receiver, lining up the slot in the bolt with the ejector. Do not push it in further than halfway.

Insert the operating lever into the receiver and engage its end in the slot at the front of the bolt. If the bolt went in too far and the slot will not line up, hold the rifle level and push the bolt back slightly with a cleaning rod from the muzzle end. If the bolt is not far enough in, other internal parts get in the way of the lever.
Line up the holes in the operating lever and the trigger plate, insert the pivot screw, and tighten it until it is snug.
On a short-action rifle, return the magazine tube under the barrel and latch it by pressing it in and turning it. Refit the thread protector if the rifle has one.
fncheck: With the rifle unloaded and pointed in a safe direction, cycle it several times by closing and then opening the action with the operating lever, and confirm it runs smoothly. Look into the ejection port and check the firing pin is not protruding from the bolt face. Finish with the lever closed, the cross-bolt safety fully right in NO-FIRE and the hammer lowered to half-cock under thumb control. If the rifle does not function correctly after assembly, Smith & Wesson says to return it to the factory for inspection and repair.
